claims.text: The dynamic mechanical response of as-cast Co-free FeNiCrMn is governed by localized adiabatic shear bands.
Activation of adiabatic shear bands in FeNiCrMn depends on strain rate and temperature.
Adiabatic shear bands enhance dislocation mobility.
Adiabatic shear bands enhance work hardening.
Shear-band-mediated dislocation processes maintain the strength–ductility balance of FeNiCrMn.
The as-cast FeNiCrMn material is single-phase or near-single-phase and has a homogeneous microstructure.
A matrix of tension and compression tests spanning quasi-static to high strain rates and cryogenic to elevated temperatures can test the hypothesis.
Using specimens with the same as-cast processing history is intended to isolate strain-rate and temperature effects.
Adiabatic shear bands locally refine the microstructure.
High strain rates and/or elevated temperatures cause deformation to localize into transient adiabatic shear bands.
Rapid local adiabatic heating inside shear bands enhances dislocation mobility.
High-rate deformation produces additional dislocation nucleation or multiplication and substantial strain hardening.
High-temperature, high-strain-rate deformation can retain high ductility and strain-hardening capacity.
At low strain rates, deformation is more uniform and produces less local temperature rise.
Increasing strain rate increases dynamic yield strength.
Elevated temperature together with high strain rate increases dynamic yield strength through shear-band-induced strain hardening.
The predicted increase in dynamic strength occurs without a severe loss of ductility.
Lower strain rates or lower temperatures produce more homogeneous deformation and relatively lower dynamic yield strength.
Quasi-static room-temperature FeNiCrMn exhibits homogeneous deformation, standard work hardening, and no pronounced shear bands.
The transition thresholds may depend on grain size, residual defects, and minor compositional inhomogeneity.
